namespace Erdos540

/-- A finite set has a non-empty subset whose sum is zero. -/
def HasZeroSubsetSum {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G] (A : Finset G) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset G, S ⊆ A ∧ S.Nonempty ∧ S.sum id = 0

/--
Is it true that if $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ has size $\gg N^{1/2}$ then there exists
some non-empty $S\subseteq A$ such that $\sum_{n\in S}n\equiv 0\pmod{N}$?

Szemerédi proved the answer is yes, in fact for arbitrary finite abelian groups.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos540.lean"]
theorem erdos_540 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (N : ℕ), 0 < N → ∀ A : Finset (ZMod N),
        C * Real.sqrt N ≤ A.card →
          HasZeroSubsetSum A := by
  sorry

end Erdos540

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a weak size inequality for every positive modulus. The theorem on p. 227 of [Sz70], specialized to cyclic groups, uses a strict size inequality and only sufficiently large moduli. These are equivalent ways to make the source’s order-sqrt(N) threshold precise.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given the eventual strict formulation with c > 0 and cutoff n₀, choose C = c + n₀ + 1. For 1 ≤ N ≤ n₀, |A| ≤ N ≤ n₀ < C ≤ C√N, so the new size hypothesis is impossible. For N > n₀, C√N ≤ |A| implies c√N < |A|, permitting application of the source statement. Conversely, the uniform weak formulation implies the eventual strict formulation with cutoff 0 and the same constant. This exact iff was proved as szemeredi_source_threshold_equiv in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the repository’s sorry theorem.
